parsed.study_design: Quantitative secondary-data spatial overlay and descriptive analysis
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents of 24 drought-prone urban villages across six districts of Semarang City; population, poverty, water-supply coverage, and other administrative data were analyzed at village and district levels.
parsed.exposure: Institutional and governance arrangements for water provision and drought management, including PDAM network coverage, community-based PAMSIMAS supply, water-truck assistance, government regulation and budgets, and implementation of rainwater harvesting and other WSUD initiatives.
parsed.outcome: Access to and availability of clean water, including piped-service coverage, reliance on community systems or rivers and wells, household water-purchasing burden, and capacity to meet increased pandemic-related water demand.
parsed.rationale: Section 2.2 (pp. 77–78) identifies a quantitative design using government administrative data and spatial overlays to assess water provision and drought vulnerability. Sections 3.2–3.3 (pp. 80–84) report that piped PDAM service did not reach the drought-prone areas, describe household reliance on alternative sources and water purchases, and empirically assess government and community drought-management initiatives, regulatory gaps, budgets, and maintenance constraints.
